diagnosis: The calibrated HBV model reaches a daily NSE of 0.812 over 1971–1997, with KGE 0.905, bias about 0.05% and r 0.91. Ivel at Blunham is a slow lowland catchment that gets much of its flow from the chalk and sand aquifers. The calibration reflects this: soil storage is large (FC about 430 mm, LP 0.62, BETA 2.3), percolation is steady (PERC about 0.95 mm/d) and the lower store recedes slowly (K2 about 0.03). The upper-store parameters (K1 0.17, K0 0.10, UZL 3.8) and MAXBAS 2.8 shape the moderate storm peaks. I set the initial soil and groundwater stores near their long-term levels so the start of the run is not distorted. Main weaknesses: (1) the slow seasonal groundwater behaviour is simplified to a single linear store, so multi-year droughts (e.g. 1976 and 1990–92) and the recessions that follow are probably not captured well; (2) sharp summer storm peaks from urban and clay areas are under-represented. The snow parameters are poorly identified because almost no precipitation falls as snow here. SFCF sits at its upper limit (1.6), which probably makes up for a small shortfall in winter water rather than describing real snow. Two separate DDS searches reached similar values for the main soil and response parameters (NSE 0.803 vs 0.812), so I am fairly confident in the parameters. I expect validation NSE around 0.7–0.8.
